rules.reason: signed-in users manage their own time logs

the timer start/stop/running routes are public execute, same convention as every other site object (app-theme's site_style, app-catalog's site_stock); the object itself requires a signed-in identity and scopes every read/write to $user_id before touching time_logs, same as the row-filtered collection API would

approving time means reading and moving somebody else's entry, which the owner-filtered rule above deliberately cannot do. The hook still refuses self-approval, so a manager approving their OWN hours is blocked by the gate rather than by this grant -- the rule says who may act on other people's time, not who may bless their own.
anyone logging time should be able to see the rate their hours will be billed at; a rate you cannot look up is one you cannot check an invoice against
writing a rate card is setting a price, not recording work
